Read a Statistics Canada table as published

Source: R/indigenous.R
sctidy.Rd

Tidies a Statistics Canada full-table download (the “CSV for database loading” form, as the data service mirrors it under statcan_indigenous/tbl_<pid>): VALUE as a number, and the quality flags kept beside it in quality.

Usage

sctidy(x)

Arguments

x

A data frame read from a Statistics Canada table (English-language full-table CSV), or a key of the data service ("statcan_indigenous/tbl_13100924", or the eight-digit table id alone). A key needs a data service key: sign in once with dlogin (see dload); a data frame you read yourself needs none.

Value

The data frame with VALUE numeric and a factor column quality with levels "ok", "E", "F", "x", "..", "...", of class c("rmbl_statcan", "data.frame").

Details

Statistics Canada flags every estimate: E use with caution, F too unreliable to be published, x suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act, .. not available, ... not applicable. An F, x, .. or ... cell has no value here (NA), whatever the file holds, and nothing in the package imputes it or works it back from totals and margins: a suppressed cell is suppressed to protect people, and small First Nations, Metis and Inuit communities most of all. E values are kept and marked.

The census data tables (98-10-xxxx) come in a wide layout: one column per member of a dimension ("Indigenous identity (9):Inuk (Inuit)[6]"), each followed by its Symbol column, and no VALUE. They are made long first: the dimension becomes a column of member labels ("Indigenous identity (9)"), the values VALUE and the symbols STATUS, so every Statistics Canada table reads the same way.

A label that names two members of one dimension (the census tables repeat labels under different parents, and the file drops the hierarchy) gets its member number from the coordinate: "Without children [3]" and "Without children [7]". Other labels are left as they are.

References

Statistics Canada. Symbol legend. statcan.gc.ca/en/concepts/definitions/guide-symbol

See also

indgap, indtabs.

Examples

# the layout of a downloaded table, with one cell suppressed
d <- data.frame(REF_DATE = "2019/2022", GEO = "Canada",
                `Indigenous identity` = c("First Nations", "Inuk (Inuit)",
                                          "Non-Indigenous"),
                VALUE = c("45.8", "", "61.5"), STATUS = c("", "x", ""),
                check.names = FALSE)
sctidy(d)
#> ╭── Statistics Canada table, tidied ──────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Rows               3                                                  │
#> │   Columns            6                                                  │
#> │   Reference periods  2019/2022                                          │
#> │   Geographies        Canada                                             │
#> │   Quality            ok 2, x 1                                          │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   REF_DATE   GEO     Indigenous identity  VALUE  quality                │
#> │   ---------  ------  -------------------  -----  -------                │
#> │   2019/2022  Canada  First Nations        45.80  ok                     │
#> │   2019/2022  Canada  Inuk (Inuit)                x                      │
#> │   2019/2022  Canada  Non-Indigenous       61.50  ok                     │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   VALUE is numeric; a suppressed cell (F, x, .., ...) is NA, with its   │
#> │   flag kept in quality.                                                 │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   Symbols: E use with caution; F too unreliable to be published;        │
#> │   x suppressed (confidentiality); .. not available; ... not applicable. │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# needs a data service key: sign in once with dlogin()
t924 <- sctidy("13100924")
}
